tagline: Eleven routes follow the West Branch past covered timber and fractured sandstone
intro: The West Branch Susquehanna River Scenic Byway links Cherry Tree and Karthaus over 72 miles, largely following the river along eleven routes. Its landmarks include McGees Mills Covered Bridge, Bilger’s Rocks and Curwensville Lake. PennDOT records its byway designation as effective July 7, 2011. River cliffs between Lumber City and Curwensville and sandstone outcrops below Bells Landing give the valley a visible geological thread. Near Grampian, the landscape is threaded with hills, mountains and river valleys. Curwensville Lake occupies another part of the river corridor, formed by a dam built after repeated floods affected Curwensville and Clearfield.

The corridor carried travelers and timber before it became a scenic drive. At Cherry Tree, canoe travelers had to carry their boats beyond the river’s navigable limit. Farther downstream, Curwensville prospered through the lumber trade. The modern designation brought together numbered highways and local roads, including Bilger’s Rocks Road; a further section of Route 879 was designated in 2012.

Begin at Cherry Tree near the headwaters, then continue toward the covered bridge west of Mahaffey. Bilger’s Rocks lies near Grampian, followed by the Curwensville area and Clearfield downstream. Beyond Clearfield, Route 879 leads through Frenchville toward Karthaus.

moments.title: Cherry Tree
moments.text: Cherry Tree was first known as Canoe Place: this was where the West Branch stopped being navigable and canoe travelers had to portage. A large cherry tree at the mouth of Cush Cushion Creek later gave the town its name. The tree marked the eastern end of the purchase line for territory the Penn family acquired from the Six Nations of the Iroquois in the 1768 Treaty of Fort Stanwix. After the tree washed away, three adjoining counties commissioned surveyors in 1849 to locate its former site. A 35-foot granite column was unveiled in 1894; the monument stands at Maple and Front streets on Route 580.

moments.title: McGees Mills Covered Bridge
moments.text: The West Branch passes beneath a wooden Burr truss covered bridge near Mahaffey. McGees Mills Covered Bridge dates to 1873 and spans 109 feet. It is among Pennsylvania’s rebuilt covered bridges, west of Mahaffey near U.S. 219. The bridge joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1988.

moments.title: Bilger's Rocks
moments.text: Passageways, arches and crawlspaces interrupt the sandstone at Bilger’s Rocks near Grampian. The remaining sandstone bed is more than 50 feet thick, exposed after softer rock above it eroded away. Mountain-building forces fractured the rock into joints. Water enters those cracks, and freezing and thawing push the rock farther apart. Plants and trees grow through the crevices, exerting pressure that enlarges the gaps. These are rocks of the Homewood Formation, whose outcrops also appear along the West Branch valley below Bells Landing. The park’s passages are part of that wider landscape of exposed sandstone.
moments.notice: Look for arches and narrow passages between fractured sandstone blocks.
